decisions.executionNote: Holder is on the right, so prepare right-hand side grasp; left arm stays home. Gradual mirrored wrist reorientation to preserve elbow-up continuity.
Approach the holder from its right side, leveling the right gripper and maintaining open jaws. Target remains outside the holder until visual alignment.
Replanned from executed prefix with smaller translation and rotation increments after continuity rejection. Continue right-side approach.
Reduce yaw change near wrist continuity limit; advance slowly with nearly fixed orientation before resuming lateral alignment.
Use an oblique front-right grasp rather than forcing the wrist through a singular side-on orientation; move toward holder with open fingers.
Fine-align right fingers around the holder and close. Holder may have shifted during approach; retention will be checked visually before transport.
The holder tipped rather than seating between the jaws. Release and withdraw slightly upward to obtain a clear view for a centered recovery grasp.
Approach the now-horizontal holder along its length, keeping the jaws open above its sidewalls. Use calibrated head geometry and stop above contact for refinement.
Lower open fingers around the horizontal holder body, then begin closing without translating. Need visual confirmation of a centered grasp.
Close fully and lift the recovered holder vertically. Check that it follows before rotating its open end upward.
Holder follows the lift. Maintain closed grasp and begin tipping its far/open end upward while moving inward with clearance.
Replan from measured pose after interruption, using slower tilt and inward translation while keeping the holder closed in the right hand.
Tilt tracking is limited in the forward posture. Retract and raise the held holder at fixed measured orientation to free wrist range before further uprighting.
Use a small bridging target consistent with the last accepted wrist configuration, then retract and raise in smaller increments.
Raise and retract the retained holder to a less constrained elbow-up posture, preserving its current orientation and closed grasp.
With the holder visibly retained, tilt its far open end upward in small increments and bring it toward the central right workspace.
Continue the upright recovery more slowly and lower the holder to a reachable working height; maintain closed right fingers.
Wrist tracking indicates a configuration constraint. Pause the tilt and move upward/forward with fixed orientation to obtain more elbow-up rotation margin.
Bring the retained holder toward the center without further wrist tilt. Prepare the left hand for a temporary supporting side grasp so the right can recover a better upright hold.
Advance the left hand upward in its own workspace, aligning its open jaws for an oblique side support of the holder; right hand stays fixed and closed.
Continue left-side support approach, matching the tilted holder axis while keeping the arms separated and right grasp fixed.
Move the left jaws above the right fingers to support the upper holder side, avoiding gripper overlap. Right hand continues holding.
Close the supporting left fingers and lower both hands together slightly to restore a clear head view; holder retention is uncertain after contact.
Holder has fallen back to the table. Separate open hands and reorient for a fresh, clear approach rather than continuing the failed support grasp.
Use smaller left wrist increments after the continuity rejection. Continue separating and leveling the open hands for a fresh recovery.
Prepare overhead grasps: right hand above the fallen holder and left above the pens. Reorient gradually while staying in each arm's workspace.
Finish orienting both open grippers downward while approaching the left cyan pen and the right holder from above; stop before grasping for visual alignment.
Replan with the right wrist fixed after the continuity guard. Lower open jaws toward the holder sides and finish left pen alignment with small increments.
Close around the centered cyan pen and the holder sidewalls, then make a short vertical lift to check both grasps visually.
Left cyan pen appears retained; lift it clear. Right grasp missed, so reopen and correct forward/downward toward the holder body.
Use wrist view to advance the right jaws onto the holder side and close. Begin tipping the retained cyan pen upright with the left hand, well clear of the table.
Right forward reach was rejected. Shift laterally and slightly back/up to retain joint margin, then close around the visible near holder edge. Continue left pen uprighting.
Lift and retract the right-hand edge grasp to check holder retention in a less extended posture. Continue rotating the held cyan pen upright.
Holder remains on the table. Change the right approach to a shallower forward-reaching angle with open jaws, while finishing the left pen's upright orientation.
Advance the right fingertips onto the holder body using the shallower approach, then close in place. Turn the upright cyan pen toward the shared working area.
Lift the right-hand edge grasp without twisting to check retention. Keep the cyan pen closed and continue orienting it for insertion.
Holder is farther forward than the previous grasp. Use a nearly horizontal open-jaw approach to reach its near side without extending the wrist as far forward.
Fine advance along the holder axis and lower the right fingers around its near sidewalls, then close without further motion. Left pen stays secured.
Retract and lift the right edge grasp without rotation, bringing the holder into reach if retained. Keep the left cyan pen stationary and closed.
The holder slipped. Align the right gripper along the holder's long axis and approach lower around its near end, avoiding another push on the upper edge.
Wrist image places the holder left of the finger center. Correct laterally and lower to its mid-height, then close around the near body.
Use a small upward/forward correction after the continuity guard, close on the near holder end, and test retention with a short retracting lift.
Raise the right jaws to the holder's mid-height before advancing; previous closures appear below its near body. Close only after this vertical correction.
Test the corrected holder grasp by retracting and lifting gently with the right gripper closed; left pen remains upright and stationary.
No movement executed in the rejected lift. Replan with much smaller retracting increments to leave the extended configuration while preserving the grasp.
Correct the lateral offset visible in the right wrist view: shift rightward in world coordinates and slightly down/forward, then close around the holder near end.
The wrist view still shows the holder outside the pinch center. Move open jaws leftward and deeper around the near end, then hold the closed target to allow settling.
Avoid further forward extension after the guard. Turn the open right fingertips toward the holder's near end at fixed wrist position, then close and settle.
Seat the jaws slightly lower on the near holder end, close, and gently retract along the table before lifting so a shallow grasp can bring it into reach.
Change to a right-side approach across the diagonal holder rather than reaching along its end at full extension. Withdraw open fingers and move rightward with gradual yaw.
Advance the right-side open jaws toward the holder center at a fixed oblique orientation. Keep the held cyan pen clear and stationary.
Make a small wrist-image lateral correction toward the visible holder side and close in place. Verify its motion before any larger transport.
Reorient the right jaw closing direction across the holder's shorter cross-section rather than its length, with a small upward clearance and lateral centering.
Center the holder in the rotated right wrist view with a small diagonal correction, then close across its short dimension. Left pen remains held.
Replan away from the rejected low wrist target: retract slightly and tip the open fingers downward toward the holder instead, then close.
Test the near-edge contact with a very small closed-gripper retracting lift, avoiding further forward extension.
The lift was rejected before motion. Start with submillimeter retraction to leave the near-singular extended posture, then gradually increase the step size.
The holder did not follow the lift. Reopen and correct the right jaw center laterally toward the near holder face, using small increments near the configuration limit.
Level the right jaw closing direction to avoid the table, then advance the open fingertips slightly deeper around the holder rather than closing at its edge.
Replan with a slight retraction and upward aiming correction so the right fingertips contact the holder body rather than its underside. Close and pause for visual confirmation.
The holder lies to the right of the pinch center in the wrist image. Aim the open fingertips rightward with a small yaw correction rather than extending the arm farther.
Test the corrected right grasp with a very small retracting lift, increasing increments gradually to avoid the nearby continuity limit.
Aim the open right jaws farther toward the holder body seen to the right of the wrist center, with a small outward correction for reach margin, then close.
Let the right fingers settle around the visible holder side, then test retention with a small, gradually increasing retracting lift while keeping both grips closed.
Reopen and move the right wrist leftward within its workspace while pitching the fingertips down toward the holder mid-body; the last closure remained above/outside the holder.
Replan the interrupted approach with submillimeter translation and much smaller wrist increments, keeping the open fingertips aimed at the holder without forcing a joint jump.
Keep orientation fixed after the guard and make a small diagonal correction into the near holder body, then close without moving the left pen.
The inward correction executed no motion. Retract from the reach limit and partially level the right wrist before trying a different holder contact.
Both previous replans executed zero steps. Use a fixed-orientation submillimeter retraction to exit the continuity boundary before any further aiming changes.
Withdraw the empty right gripper to regain substantial reach margin and a clear view, preserving orientation and the left-hand pen grasp.
Reorient the empty right fingers toward an overhead approach at the retracted position, using small angular increments and monitoring continuity before translating.
Lower the right wrist while bringing the open fingertips toward a shallower near-end grasp, using coordinated small increments rather than extending overhead beyond reach.
Right tracking shows a joint boundary. Raise the empty wrist and adjust its pitch gradually to recover configuration margin before another grasp attempt; left pen remains secured.
Replan from the measured interrupted pose with quarter-scale increments to recover the right elbow configuration without forcing a joint jump. Keep left pen held.
Change to a more lateral right-side approach to recover reach margin: move the wrist toward its shoulder while aiming the open fingertips inward at the holder.
The lateral replan executed zero steps. Reduce each increment to one quarter near the continuity boundary, keeping the fingers open.
Continue the accepted lateral approach, gradually lowering the open fingertips toward the holder while keeping the wrist closer to the right shoulder.
Advance the open right jaws diagonally toward the holder, with a slight rise rather than lowering into the reach boundary. Stop on any continuity interruption.
Forward extension was interrupted. Replan by lowering the wrist and leveling the open fingers, gaining fingertip reach without moving the wrist farther forward.
Continue the accepted lowering-and-leveling path, bringing the open right fingertips to the holder sidewall height with only a small forward advance.
Correct toward the holder on the right side of the wrist image, then close at its side. If contact holds, draw the holder nearer before trying to lift.
Forward motion was rejected. At the current reach, roll the open jaws toward a top-bottom pinch of the holder's short height, with slight clearance and no further extension.
Close the angled right jaws on the holder near end and let contact settle, then test a tiny retracting lift. The holder appears closer to the pinch region now.
The holder did not follow. Reopen and angle the fingertips downward at fixed wrist position to reach the holder's lower side instead of closing above it.
The angled lower jaw appears table-limited. Lift slightly and roll the open jaws toward a horizontal pinch while correcting toward the holder in the wrist view.
Lower the leveled right jaws toward the holder sidewall while retracting slightly for reach margin. Use small fixed-orientation increments near the continuity boundary.
The wrist view shows the holder above the finger pinch region after lowering. Correct upward and slightly inward with open jaws, using small increments.
Use the observed wrist-image response to raise the pinch region onto the holder side and correct laterally toward its center, then close in place.
Forward translation reached the guard. Keep the wrist fixed and aim the fingertips upward/rightward toward the holder visible in the wrist image, then close.
The holder is now within the right finger region. Keep the closed target, let contact settle, then make a small retracting lift to test actual retention.
